Home.description: See them smile again, be moved, sing, learn —and, why not, cry too— surrounded by the people they love, in moments none of you will forget.

hero.imageAlt: A cellist performs for a group of patients and family members in a hospital common room, with a person in a wheelchair among the audience.

mission.title: One open slot in the schedule can be the best moment of the month.
mission.description: We don't replace care — we accompany it. We coordinate with each centre so music, theatre, or a workshop arrives without interrupting care, and so every performance means something to the person receiving it.
mission.imageAlt: An artist shows coloured paper cut-outs to a group of patients, a teenager, and a nurse gathered around a table covered in craft materials.

trust.title: Every slot is opened by a care centre, not an anonymous platform.
trust.description: Coordinators at each centre review and confirm proposals before they reach the people in their care. That's how Todo el tiempo cuenta stays safe and meaningful.

closing.title: Ready to open the first slot, or propose the first moment?
closing.description: Centres and artists register in the same place. A coordinator reviews every profile before it can act.

what.eyebrow: What Todo el tiempo cuenta is
what.title: Live culture to accompany the wait.
what.description: We connect care centres with artists to fill waiting hours with music, workshops, and live performances. Free for everyone. Non-profit.

Help.title: How Todo el tiempo cuenta works
Help.intro: A quick guide to the process, for centres, artists, and families.

howItWorks.title: How a moment comes together
howItWorks.description: Four steps, one shared afternoon. Before any of it begins, an administrator validates every centre and every artist; after that, each step is reviewed before it reaches the people who'll receive it.

01.text: Open a slot in the centre's agenda — a date, a time, a place where the people there could use some company.

02.text: Browse open slots and propose an activity: music, storytelling, magic, a workshop.

03.text: The same centre reviews the proposals it received and confirms one. The moment becomes a scheduled event.

04.text: The people there and their families see what's coming up.

items.question: How are events rated?
items.answer: Only signed-in users can rate, and the only sign-up is for care centres and artists, so families and visitors cannot rate yet. A signed-in user can rate a published event from 1 to 5 stars and change the rating later. Each event shows only the average and the number of ratings, never who rated.

items.question: What do a slot's age bands (audience) mean?
items.answer: Each slot a centre publishes shows a rough age band — for example ages 0–5, 6–12, adults, or all ages — so artists can propose an activity suited to who'll attend.

items.question: How is people's location protected?
items.answer: The platform does not record the name, location or reason for stay of the people being cared for. Public pages show the name and city of the centre hosting each event, never its room or street address. A slot's room or space is visible only to signed-in artists with an approved profile, while the slot is open; it never appears on public pages. Event titles and descriptions are public and written by the centres, who are asked not to include rooms or personal details.

About.title: A non-profit platform bringing live culture to the places where care keeps people away from home.
About.intro: Here we explain what Todo el tiempo cuenta is, who takes part, how privacy is protected, and why it's free. For a step-by-step of how to publish or propose, visit Help.

purpose.title: Our purpose
purpose.description: Long stays and days away from home isolate. Todo el tiempo cuenta exists so music, theatre, and workshops reach the care centre without replacing care, always coordinated with the centre itself.

items.name: People and family

flow.title: The journey, at a glance
flow.description: A slot starts at the centre, an artist proposes for it, and it becomes a public event. For the detail of each step, see Help.

validation.title: Validated profiles
validation.description: No centre or artist can act on the platform until an admin reviews and approves their profile. That validation is what keeps Todo el tiempo cuenta safe and meaningful.

dataStance.title: What data we publish, and what we don't
dataStance.description: Centres and events are public, and each event names the centre that hosts it. We publish only what is needed to find them: for a centre, its name, city, postal code, centre type, map position and number of upcoming events; for an event, its title, description, date, duration, artist, audience, capacity, average rating and number of ratings, and the host centre's name and city.
excluded: The exact room or space where an event takes place
The content of proposals between centres and artists
Email addresses and the identifiers of accounts, profiles or slots
Data about the people being cared for (the platform does not record it)
dataStance.note: A slot's room or space is visible only to signed-in artists with an approved profile, while the slot is open, and never appears on public pages. Event titles and descriptions are written by the centres, who are asked not to include rooms or personal details; they are not checked automatically.

funding.title: Why it's free
funding.description: Todo el tiempo cuenta is a non-profit initiative. Centres, artists, and families pay nothing to take part; the project is sustained apart from any transaction between them.
